title: Armistice Day and piano player Tom Zimmerman
summary: On Armistice Day the Grunewald manager asked for the band at noon; his wife filled in on piano, and he praises pianist Tom Zimmerman.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: My daughter is an excellent pianist. My wife was an excellent pianist. I remember... And this is way back. When this... Armistice Day... Now I am going back. Armistice Day? World War One? Yeah. Mr. Gruenwald said... Not Mr. Weiss. Mr. Gruenwald. The Gruenwald said... Johnny! If possible get the band together. I said it's the middle of the day. He said well get them... Get something. We're going to have a celebration here. Armistice is having to sign at 11 o'clock. I'd like to hear the band at 12 o'clock. Well I worked fast. I dug up everybody but the piano. So I asked Mrs. D. Duarte to play the piano for me. And she's sitting up there in a powder blue dress with a big powder blue hat. You know how to dress in the old days. And all the girls come up throwing their arms around my neck with my wife sitting at the piano.

You know? Well then after a while in comes my piano player, Tom Zimmerman, one of the greatest, I can't tell you how great he was and couldn't read a note as big as a customer. When he played he was Frankie Call and another Frankie Call. My idea of a rhythm piano player, I mean clean playing, was Frankie Call. Did you ever hear Frankie Call? Sure. Didn't he have a touch? Beautiful. And melodic too.
